slug: 凡人修仙疯了吧你百岁高龄才入门
lines: 苍莽群山，层峦叠嶂。
山脚下的葫芦村，炊烟袅袅，岁月静谧，与世隔绝数百年，从未出过一名修士，世世代代皆是面朝黄土的凡人，生老病死，难逃轮回。
村头老槐树下，坐着一位垂垂老矣的老者。
老者名唤苏玄尘，今日，是他整整一百岁的寿辰。
满头白发如雪，枯瘦的脸上布满沟壑纵横的皱纹，眼皮松弛耷拉，一双眼眸浑浊黯淡，早已没了半分年轻人的神采。佝偻的身躯撑不起单薄的粗布麻衣，微风拂过，衣袂飘摇，仿佛一阵大风，便能将这百岁老翁吹倒在地。
无人知晓，苏玄尘并非此土原生之人。
他是一名穿越者。
距今整整八十二年，他从繁华盛世的现代，猝不及防降临这个仙道昌盛、凡人如草芥的修真世界。
初来之时，他尚且年少，满心憧憬，以为手握穿越者优势，定能踏仙路、求长生，挣脱凡人的宿命。
可现实，狠狠击碎了他所有的幻想。
他无灵根、无仙缘、无奇遇，是最最普通的凡躯，天生与仙道绝缘。
年少相伴的未婚妻白芷，天资出众，年少便测出中品木灵根。八十二年之前，仙门巡仙修士路过村落，遴选门徒，白芷一朝被选中，一步踏入仙途。
临别之时，年少佳人眉眼清冷，只留一句冰冷刺骨的话语，萦绕苏玄尘心头，整整百年未曾消散。
“苏玄尘，你我仙凡有别，从此陌路，再无瓜葛。”
一语断情，一语隔世。
自此，白芷乘风而去，御剑飞天，踏入无数凡人梦寐以求的仙门，扶摇直上。
而苏玄尘，困于凡俗，困于无灵根的桎梏。
八十二年光阴，弹指即过。
他娶妻生子，目送双亲老去、妻儿离世、邻里更迭。身边的人来来去去，悉数化作一抔黄土，唯有他，靠着远超常人的体魄，孤零零熬到了百岁高龄。
百年岁月，看透生老病死，看惯世事无常。
如今的苏玄尘，亲朋尽逝，孑然一身，只剩满身风霜，和一颗早已看淡红尘，却依旧藏着一丝不甘的心。
他的怀中，常年揣着一本泛黄古朴的旧书。
这是他穿越而来唯一的伴身之物，八十二年以来，书页陈旧，字迹模糊，看上去与寻常古籍别无二致，从未展现过半分神异。久而久之，苏玄尘也早已将其当做普通旧物，随身带在身边。
“一百岁了啊……”
苏玄尘低声呢喃，声音沙哑干涩，带着无尽沧桑。
凡人寿元，不过七十古来稀，他能活至百岁，已是天幸，烛火垂暮，寿元已然见底。按照身体状态，最多只剩半年阳寿，便要灯枯油尽，埋骨青山。
这辈子，终究是个凡人。
他曾无数次仰望天际，看着偶尔划过天际的御剑流光，看着仙人腾云驾雾、逍遥自在，心中满是艳羡与落寞。
仙凡之别，何止天堑。
就在苏玄尘闭目静待余生落幕之时，一阵清脆的鹤鸣自天际传来，划破了葫芦村百年的宁静。
清风流云分开，两道白衣身影御空而来，踏虚而立，身姿飘逸，仙气缭绕。
是青玄宗的巡仙修士！
方圆百里，唯一的正统仙门，每三年下山一次，遍历村落，遴选有灵根的孩童，收入门下，培育仙苗。
整个葫芦村的村民瞬间沸腾，老少皆跪，叩首朝拜，眼神中满是极致的敬畏与向往。
仙人，是他们此生只能仰望的存在。
两名青玄宗女修落至村口，身姿清冷，气质出尘，不染凡尘。一人手持拂尘，一人捧着一枚莹白剔透的玉盘，正是测灵专用的探玄玉。
“规矩照旧，六岁至十六岁孩童，依次上前测灵，有灵根者，随我回山，无灵根者，原地退下。”
清冷的仙音落下，村民们连忙驱赶着家中孩童上前排队。
一个个稚嫩的孩童伸手触碰探玄玉，玉盘平平无奇，毫无反应。
无灵根。
接连二十余个孩童，尽数皆是凡躯，无一人有修仙资质。
负责测灵的年轻女修眉头微蹙，眼中带着几分不耐。
“又是一个无灵根的贫瘠村落，白白浪费时间。”
content_en:
The vast mountains are layered upon layers of mountains.
The Hulu Village at the foot of the mountain is filled with smoke and quiet time. It has been isolated from the world for hundreds of years. There has never been a monk. For generations, they are all mortals facing the loess. They are born, old, sick and die, and cannot escape the cycle of reincarnation.
Under the old locust tree at the head of the village, there was an old man sitting.
The old man's name is Su Xuanchen, and today is his 100th birthday.
His hair was as white as snow, his skinny face was covered with furrows and wrinkles, his eyelids were loose and droopy, his eyes were cloudy and dim, and he had lost half of his youthful look. The rickety body could not hold up the thin coarse linen clothes. The breeze blew and the clothes were swaying, as if a strong wind could blow the centenarian old man to the ground.
No one knew that Su Xuanchen was not a native of this land.
He is a time traveler.
Exactly eighty-two years ago, he came unexpectedly from the prosperous modern era to this world of cultivation where immortals are prosperous and mortals are like grass.
When he first came, he was still young and full of longing, thinking that with the advantage of being a time traveler, he would be able to walk on the path of immortality, seek immortality, and escape the fate of a mortal.
But reality severely shattered all his fantasies.
He has no spiritual roots, no immortal fate, and no adventure. He is the most ordinary mortal body, and is naturally insulated from the immortal way.
The fiancée Bai Zhi who has been with her since she was young has outstanding talent, and she was diagnosed with a medium-grade wood spirit root at a young age. Eighty-two years ago, the Immortal Sect's patrolling monks passed by the village to select disciples. Once Bai Zhi was selected, she stepped into the path of immortality.
When parting, the young beauty's eyes were cold, leaving only one cold and biting words, which lingered in Su Xuanchen's heart for a hundred years and never dissipated.
"Su Xuanchen, you and I are different from each other. From now on, we will become strangers and have nothing to do with each other."
One word cuts off love, one word separates the world.
From then on, Bai Zhi rode the wind, flew into the sky with her sword, stepped into the fairy gate that countless mortals dream of, and skyrocketed.
But Su Xuanchen was trapped in the mundane world and the shackles of having no spiritual roots.
Eighty-two years passed in a blink of an eye.
He married a wife and had children, and watched his parents grow old, his wife and children die, and his neighborhood changed. The people around him came and went, all turning into a handful of loess. Only he, relying on his physique far beyond ordinary people, survived to the age of 100 alone.
Over the course of a hundred years, I have seen through birth, aging, sickness and death, and have become accustomed to the impermanence of things in the world.
Today, Su Xuanchen has lost all his relatives and friends, and is all alone, with only a body full of wind and frost, and a heart that has long looked down on the world of mortals, but still hides a trace of unwillingness.
In his arms, he always carries a yellowed and simple old book.
This was the only thing that accompanied him when he traveled through time. Over the past eighty-two years, the pages of the book were old and the handwriting was blurred. It looked the same as an ordinary ancient book, and it had never shown anything magical. Over time, Su Xuanchen had long regarded it as an ordinary old thing and carried it with him.
"A hundred years old..."
Su Xuanchen murmured in a low voice, his voice hoarse and dry, filled with endless vicissitudes of life.
The life span of ordinary people is only seventy years old. It is rare for him to live to be a hundred years old. It is a blessing. The candlelight is dying and the life span has already bottomed out. According to the state of the body, only half a year of life is left at most, and the lamp will be exhausted and the bones will be buried in the green mountains.
In this life, he is a mortal after all.
He had looked up to the sky countless times, watching the light of his sword occasionally streaking across the sky, watching the immortals flying in the clouds and mist, carefree and at ease, and his heart was full of envy and loneliness.
The difference between immortals and mortals goes beyond the natural chasm.
Just when Su Xuanchen closed his eyes and waited for the end of the rest of his life, a clear and clear cry of cranes came from the sky, breaking the centuries-old tranquility of Hulu Village.
Buzz——
The breeze and flowing clouds parted, and two figures in white came from the sky, standing on the void, with elegant postures and fairy aura.
He is the Immortal Patrolling Monk of Qingxuan Sect!
The only orthodox fairy sect in a hundred miles radius goes down the mountain every three years, goes through the villages, selects children with spiritual roots, takes them under its sect, and cultivates fairy seedlings.
The entire village of Hulu Village was instantly excited. All young and old knelt down, kowtowed and worshiped, their eyes full of extreme awe and yearning.
Immortals are the existences they can only look up to in this life.
Two female cultivators from the Qingxuan Sect arrived at the entrance of the village. Their figures were cold and their temperament was untainted by the mundane world. One person is holding a fly whisk, and the other person is holding a white and clear jade plate, which is a mysterious jade specially used for detecting spirits.
"The rules remain as usual. Children between the ages of six and sixteen should come forward one by one to test their spirits. Those with spiritual roots should follow me back to the mountain. Those without spiritual roots should stay where they are."
As the cold fairy music fell, the villagers quickly drove their children forward to line up.
One by one, the immature children stretched out their hands to touch the Tanxuan Jade, but the jade plate was unremarkable and showed no reaction.
No spiritual roots.
There were more than twenty children in a row, all of them had mortal bodies, and none of them had the qualifications to become an immortal.
The young female cultivator responsible for soul testing frowned slightly, with a hint of impatience in her eyes.
"Another barren village without spiritual roots, a waste of time."
